item.title: Seamless remote coding sessions
item.description:
I do my remote development from iTerm2 on my Mac, with the code, development services and coding sessions running on a Linux machine at home.

A few incredibly useful tools make this a perfect, seamless setup for remote work sessions with intermittend network access. I’m in the incredibly luxurious position that I can work from anywhere, and I’ve got a mini campervan, a solar panel, and Starlink Internet. My work is mostly talking to coding agents and babysitting them through development tasks, which means I can do a bunch of planning work, kick off a long, uninterrupted development task, and in the meantime I can drive from one beautiful place to the next. After arriving, I open my laptop and I can resume work immediately, as if I’m working locally.

item.title: small useful git tricks
item.description:
Here’s a couple of git aliases I use all the time. It gives you a quick and clear overview of your branches and commits. It can even watch for changes in realtime and show you any changes.

A better git log

Add this to your .gitconfig:

1
2

[alias]
 tree = log --graph --decorate --all --format='%C(auto)%h%d %Creset%s %C(dim)(%an, %ad)%Creset' --date=relative

Run git tree and you get a compact view of your commit history with branches, colored hashes, commit messages, and authors. The --all flag shows all branches, not just the current one.
